mainTopic: When a windpipe is severed during שחיטה, is the animal a נבלה or a טרפה? Several answers to the clash between the sources, followed by ריש לקיש's ruling about a punctured lung and how far it reaches.
overview: The גמרא has just said that רבי עקיבא changed his mind and agreed with רבי ישבב: an animal that becomes unfit during its שחיטה is a נבלה. It challenges this from the משנה in אלו טרפות, which calls a severed windpipe only a טרפה. רבא first answers that the order of the cuts matters. רב אחא בר הונא knocks that down from a ברייתא, so רבא answers instead that the משנה is a general list of forbidden animals: some on it are נבלות and some are טרפות. The list leaves out נבלות that are already טמא while alive, like the cases of חזקיה and רבי אלעזר. ריש לקיש offers a different answer, based on whether the gullet was cut at the same spot as the windpipe's cut. That answer is challenged from his own ruling about a punctured lung. Finally רבי יוחנן explains that one משנה is from before רבי עקיבא's retraction and one from after, and a משנה is not moved from its place. The גמרא then studies ריש לקיש's lung ruling: רבא limits it to the lung, רבי זירא objects but takes his objection back, and the גמרא begins comparing רבי זירא's question to אילפא's question about a fetus.

steps.title: The משנה lists a severed windpipe as a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge by quoting the משנה in אלו טרפות. That משנה calls a perforated gullet and a severed windpipe טרפות, not נבלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה lists: an animal with a perforated gullet, or with a severed windpipe [as a טרפה]!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה that seems to contradict what it just said. It claimed that רבי עקיבא agreed with רבי ישבב, yet this משנה calls a severed windpipe only a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישבב holds that if an animal becomes unfit during its שחיטה, it is a נבלה. A windpipe severed improperly looks like exactly that kind of case. Yet the משנה calls it a טרפה, so the question is which תנא this משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet (food pipe)
The windpipe
Perforated, having a hole going all the way through
Severed, cut through
An animal with a fatal defect. It cannot be eaten, but it is a different status from a נבלה.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the end of the question. The first part, about רבי עקיבא agreeing with רבי ישבב, came just before. The quoted words are the 'proof' that seems to go against it.

phrases.english: A perforated gullet
and a severed windpipe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge, begun just before this text, against the claim that רבי עקיבא agreed with רבי ישבב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא retracted and agreed with רבי ישבב that an animal becoming unfit during שחיטה is a נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A severed windpipe should be a case of becoming unfit through the שחיטה. Yet the משנה calls it a טרפה, not a נבלה.

steps.title: רבא: it depends on which cut came first
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the two rulings deal with different orders of cutting. If the gullet was slaughtered first and the windpipe severed afterward, it is a נבלה. If the windpipe was severed first, it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not difficult. Here, he slaughtered first and only afterward severed. There, he severed first and only afterward slaughtered. If he slaughtered and then severed, the animal became unfit through its שחיטה. If he severed and then slaughtered, it is as if something else made it unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by splitting the cases according to the order of the cuts. רבי ישבב's נבלה ruling and the משנה's טרפה ruling are about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the gullet has been properly cut, the שחיטה is already underway. A ruined windpipe cut after that means the animal was ruined by the שחיטה itself, so it is a נבלה. If the windpipe was severed before any slaughtering began, the damage is a separate injury outside the שחיטה, so the animal is a טרפה, just as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This introduces an answer that resolves a contradiction.
And in the end, afterward
Becomes unfit through its slaughter, which makes it a נבלה
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה. It has a stricter status than a טרפה, including passing on טומאה.
Something else caused it, meaning a cause outside the שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's first answer: the order matters. Gullet first, then windpipe severed badly: נבלה. Windpipe severed badly first: טרפה. Steps 3 to 5 challenge this answer, and in step 6 רבא replaces it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is רבא's first attempt to fit רבי ישבב's rule with the משנה. It is attacked from a ברייתא in the next steps, and רבא later replaces it with a different answer.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is where he slaughtered and in the end severed;
phrases.notes: 'Slaughtered' means he properly cut the gullet. 'Severed' means the windpipe was cut through in a way that is not a proper שחיטה.

phrases.english: there, it is where he severed and in the end slaughtered.
If he slaughtered and in the end severed,
it became unfit through its slaughter;
if he severed and in the end slaughtered,
it is as though something else caused it
to become unfit.
phrases.notes: דָּמְיָא, 'it is like', goes with the word כִּי at the start of the last row: 'it is like something else made it unfit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה by separating the cases according to the order of the cuts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא by order of events)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any improper severing of the windpipe should count as becoming unfit during שחיטה, so it should be a נבלה, which clashes with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only if the gullet was slaughtered first is it a נבלה. If the windpipe was severed first, it is a טרפה, as the משנה says.

steps.title: A ברייתא calls both orders נבלה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא objects to רבא with a ברייתא. It says that whether the gullet was cut first or the windpipe was severed first, the animal is a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא objected to רבא: If one slaughtered the gullet and severed the windpipe, or severed the windpipe and afterward slaughtered the gullet, it is a נבלה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא brings a ברייתא that seems to ignore the order of the cuts. It calls both orders a נבלה, which goes against רבא's distinction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second case in the ברייתא, severing the windpipe first, is exactly the case רבא called a טרפה. The ברייתא calls it a נבלה, so it looks like order makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: He slaughtered, meaning a proper cut
He severed, meaning cut through improperly
And afterward

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Huna raised an objection to Rava:
If one slaughtered the gullet
and severed the windpipe,
or severed the windpipe
and afterward slaughtered the gullet,
it is a נבלה!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer from Step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction that severing the windpipe first makes the animal only a טרפה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly mentions severing the windpipe first and then cutting the gullet, and still calls it a נבלה.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא: the gullet was already cut first
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers by rereading the second case of the ברייתא. It does not mean the gullet was cut afterward. It means the gullet had already been cut from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: and he had already slaughtered the gullet from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his distinction by reading the ברייתא's second case differently. In that case too, the gullet was cut first, before the windpipe was severed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, both cases in the ברייתא have the gullet slaughtered first. So both are נבלה, which fits רבא's rule perfectly. The ברייתא never actually discusses a windpipe severed before any slaughtering, so רבא's טרפה case stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, read it as. This introduces a new reading of a source.
And already
From the beginning, at the outset

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is changing his rule. He keeps it exactly as it was and only shows that the ברייתא, read correctly, agrees with it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule survives: a נבלה requires that the gullet was slaughtered before the windpipe was severed.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא: וּכְבָר שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט מֵעִיקָּרָא.
phrases.english: Say: and he had already slaughtered the gullet at the outset.
phrases.notes: רבא is reading the words 'and afterward slaughtered the gullet' from the ברייתא as 'and he had already slaughtered the gullet before.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: וּכְבָר שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא בר הונא's objection by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's second case means the windpipe was severed before any slaughtering, and it is still a נבלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the ברייתא's second case, the gullet had already been slaughtered first, so it fits רבא's rule that such a case is a נבלה.

steps.title: Two refutations of רבא's rereading
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא gives two reasons why רבא cannot reread the ברייתא's second case as one where the gullet was cut from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There are two refutations of what you said. First, your reading makes the second case the same as the first case. Second, the ברייתא clearly says the gullet was cut 'afterward'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא rejects רבא's answer from step 4. He shows that the new reading of the ברייתא does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second case means the gullet was already cut first, it is the same case as the ברייתא's first case, and a ברייתא would not teach the same case twice. Also, the ברייתא actually uses the words 'and afterward,' so the windpipe really was severed first. That brings רב אחא בר הונא's objection against רבא right back.

keyTerms.meaning: Two refutations, two reasons an answer fails
The first one, here the first case in the ברייתא
And afterward

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב אחא בר הונא answering רבא.

phrases.english: There are two refutations of this matter:
One, that this is the same as the first case,
And furthermore, we learned 'and afterward'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's rereading of the ברייתא from step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's rereading of the second case in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It makes the second case repeat the first, and it goes against the ברייתא's explicit words 'and afterward'

steps.title: The list in אלו טרפות means 'forbidden', not only טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer: the משנה lists animals that are forbidden. Some of them are נבלות and some are טרפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The משנה is teaching a list of things that are forbidden. Some of them are נבלות, and some of them are טרפות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops his earlier answer about the order of cutting. He gives a completely new way to explain the משנה in אלו טרפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction was that the משנה calls a severed windpipe a טרפה, while other sources call it a נבלה. רבא now says the משנה's heading is not an exact label for each case. It is a general list of animals that may not be eaten, so a severed windpipe can be on the list and still be a real נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden animals, ones that may not be eaten
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה; it may not be eaten and it also makes things טמא
An animal with a fatal defect; it may not be eaten but does not make things טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying a severed windpipe is not a נבלה. He is saying it is a נבלה, even though it appears in a משנה whose title talks about טרפות.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It teaches: 'These are forbidden,'
and some of them are unslaughtered carcasses,
and some of them are tereifot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: אֵלּוּ אֲסוּרוֹת קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the order-of-cutting answer was knocked down, רבא offers a new answer to the original contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's heading as a general list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in אלו טרפות labels every case on its list as a טרפה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists forbidden animals in general; some items on the list, like a severed windpipe, are נבלות

steps.title: Why not list the נבלה cases of חזקיה and רבי אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה's list includes נבלות, it should also include חזקיה's case of an animal cut in half and רבי אלעזר's case of a thigh removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the משנה also list חזקיה's case, since חזקיה said: If one made the animal like a shard, it is a נבלה. And let it also list רבי אלעזר's case, since רבי אלעזר said: If the thigh and its hollow were removed, it is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's new answer. If the list includes נבלות, why are some well-known נבלה cases missing from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the משנה is a list of all forbidden animals, including נבלות, it should be complete. Yet two known נבלה rulings, from חזקיה and רבי אלעזר, do not appear on it. That makes it look like the list is not really meant to include נבלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it list, it should have counted
A shard; an animal cut into two pieces across its width
Thigh, the hind leg
The hollow space left where the thigh was removed

phrases.english: And let it also list that of Ḥizkiyya,
as Ḥizkiyya said:
If one made it like a shard, it is an unslaughtered carcass,
phrases.notes: The animal was cut into two halves across its width. It is a נבלה even while it is still moving.

phrases.english: and let it also list that of Rabbi Elazar,
as Rabbi Elazar said:
If the thigh and its hollow were removed, it is an unslaughtered carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's new answer from step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the משנה in אלו טרפות includes נבלות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the list includes נבלות, it is incomplete without the known נבלה cases of חזקיה and רבי אלעזר

steps.title: The list leaves out a נבלה that is already טמא while alive
steps.stepSummary: The משנה only lists נבלות that do not make things טמא while the animal is alive. The cases of חזקיה and רבי אלעזר do, so they are left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches a נבלה, it means one that does not make things טמא while alive. But a נבלה that makes things טמא while still alive, it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 7. It explains why חזקיה's and רבי אלעזר's cases are not on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal cut in half, or missing its thigh and hollow, already counts as a נבלה and makes things טמא even while it is still moving. A severed windpipe does not do that while the animal lives. The משנה's list covers only the second kind, so leaving out the first kind is no problem for רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things ritually impure (טמא)
While it is still alive
It does not teach, it does not include

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's final answer: the משנה in אלו טרפות is a list of forbidden animals, and a severed windpipe on it is really a נבלה. The list only includes נבלות that are not already טמא while the animal is alive, which is why חזקיה's and רבי אלעזר's cases are missing.

phrases.english: When it teaches an unslaughtered carcass,
it is one that does not impart impurity while alive,
but an unslaughtered carcass that imparts impurity while alive,
phrases.notes: These are the cases of חזקיה and רבי אלעזר from the last step.

phrases.english: it does not teach.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי נְבֵלָה, דְּלָא מְטַמְּאָה מֵחַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and protects רבא's answer from step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the משנה's list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the list includes נבלות, it should include every נבלה case
steps.terutzMaskana: The list includes only נבלות that do not make things טמא while the animal is alive

steps.title: Same spot or a different spot
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש settles the clash between the two משניות. If the gullet was cut at the same spot as the cut in the windpipe, the animal is a נבלה. If it was cut at a different spot, the animal is only a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: In one משנה, he cut the gullet at the same place as the earlier cut in the windpipe. In the other, he cut it at a different place. Cutting at the same place means the animal was ruined by the slaughter itself. Cutting at a different place is like something else ruining the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers a new way to settle the clash between our משנה and the משנה on 42a. He says the two משניות are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the slaughter cut lands on the old wound, the שחיטה itself was spoiled. That makes the animal a נבלה, the status our משנה gives. If the slaughter cut is somewhere else, the windpipe damage counts as an outside defect, so the animal is a טרפה, as the משנה on 42a says.

keyTerms.meaning: In the place of the cut: the same spot where the windpipe was already cut
It was made invalid by the slaughter itself, so it becomes a נבלה
Something else caused it to become invalid, which makes it a טרפה
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה; it makes things טמא
An animal with a fatal defect; it is forbidden to eat but does not make things טמא as a נבלה does

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
Here, it is where he cut at the place of the cut,
phrases.notes: "Here" means our משנה. The second "here" in the next line means the משנה on 42a.

phrases.english: There, it is where he cut not at the place of the cut.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ – נִפְסְלָה בִּשְׁחִיטָה הִיא,
phrases.english: If he cut at the place of the cut, it was made invalid by the slaughter;
if he cut not at the place of the cut,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי דָּבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לָהּ לִיפָּסֵל דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: it is like something else caused it to become invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: כָּאן – שֶׁשָּׁחַט בִּמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the same clash that רבא addressed in steps 6 to 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה is about a different physical case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seem to describe the same case but give it different statuses (נבלה and טרפה).
steps.terutzMaskana: Same spot means the slaughter ruined it, so it is a נבלה. A different spot means an outside defect, so it is a טרפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's own ruling about the lung contradicts him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from his own ruling. If the windpipe was cut and then the lung was punctured, the animal is kosher. That ruling treats everything tied to a cut windpipe as if it were already out of the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did ריש לקיש really say this? But he also said that if one cut the windpipe and afterward the lung was punctured, the animal is kosher. So once the windpipe is cut, it is like something lying in a basket. Here too, it should be like something lying in a basket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's answer by pointing to another ruling of his that seems to clash with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lung ruling, cutting the windpipe makes the lung count as if it were already removed, so later damage to it does not matter. By the same logic, a windpipe that was cut first should simply drop out of the picture. If so, there is no reason why the spot where the gullet is cut should change the animal's status, and ריש לקיש's distinction falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe (trachea), one of the two סימנים cut in שחיטה
The lung
Kosher, fit to eat
Apparently, so we see: draws a conclusion from a source
Like something lying in a basket: counted as already outside the animal

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי?
phrases.english: And did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say:
If he cut the windpipe
and afterward the lung was punctured, it is kosher!
So apparently it is like something lying in a basket;
phrases.notes: Once the windpipe is cut, the lung is treated as if it were already out of the animal, so a hole in it doesn't matter.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי כְּמַאן דְּמַנְּחָא בְּדִיקּוּלָא דָּמְיָא.
phrases.english: here too it should be like something lying in a basket.
phrases.notes: Here the cut windpipe itself should count as out of the picture, so where the gullet is cut shouldn't change anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's distinction between cutting at the same spot and cutting at a different spot.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inner contradiction: ריש לקיש's lung ruling treats a cut windpipe as removing it from the animal's status. That would make his spot-based distinction pointless.

steps.title: Before and after a retraction
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the two משניות reflect two stages of one opinion. One was taught before the ruling was retracted, the other after. The old משנה was simply left where it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It is not difficult. One משנה is from before the retraction, and the other is from after it. And a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: Since ריש לקיש's answer failed, the גמרא brings a completely different answer from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משניות do not have to be reconciled as two different cases. They really do disagree, because the ruling changed over time. The earlier version, which calls an animal with a cut windpipe a טרפה, stayed in the משנה even after the ruling was changed, because a משנה that was already taught is not erased.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is coming
It is not difficult: introduces an answer
A retraction, when a sage changes his ruling
A משנה does not move from its place: an earlier version stays in the text even after the ruling changes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the old משנה was a mistake that someone forgot to fix. It was deliberately left in place, even though the practical ruling follows the later version.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
It is not difficult:
one is from before the retraction,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on 42a, which calls a cut windpipe a טרפה. The retraction is רבי עקיבא changing his mind.

phrases.english: and one is from after the retraction,
and a משנה does not move from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's answer after step 10 knocked it down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two stages of one opinion: before and after a retraction.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות must agree, so the case would have to be split some other way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משניות really disagree. One reflects the earlier view, and the משנה was left unchanged after the retraction.
steps.whatToRemember: The clash between the משניות is settled historically, not by splitting the cases. One משנה is from before a retraction and one from after, and a משנה stays in its place.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's punctured-lung ruling, quoted on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now studies, for its own sake, the ruling of ריש לקיש that was quoted in step 10. If the windpipe was cut and then the lung was punctured, the animal is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: ריש לקיש said that if one cut the windpipe and afterward the lung was punctured, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to ריש לקיש's ruling, which it used earlier only as a challenge, in order to discuss it directly. This sets up רבא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 this ruling was only a tool to attack ריש לקיש's answer. Now it becomes the main topic. The גמרא repeats it word for word so it can examine how far it reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: the גמרא returns to a statement it quoted earlier in order to study it directly
It was punctured, got a hole

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
If he cut the windpipe
and afterward the lung was punctured, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ruling that was quoted in step 10 as a challenge, now to discuss it directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the windpipe is cut, a later hole in the lung does not make the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: The rule covers the lung, not the intestines
steps.stepSummary: רבא limits ריש לקיש's ruling to the lung. The lung depends on the windpipe, so cutting the windpipe takes the lung out of the picture. The intestines do not depend on the windpipe, so a hole in them still makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: ריש לקיש said this only about the lung, since the life of the lung depends on the windpipe. But with the intestines, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains how far ריש לקיש's ruling goes and where it stops.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the lung's hole does not matter is that the lung only works through the windpipe. Once the windpipe is cut, the lung counts as gone. The intestines have no such link to the windpipe, so if they are punctured before the gullet is cut, the animal becomes a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
The life of the lung depends on the windpipe
The intestines, the inner organs of the belly

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's "basket" rule depends on a link to the windpipe. It works for the lung, which depends on the windpipe, but not for the intestines, which do not.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אֶלָּא בְּרֵיאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said this only about the lung,
since the life of the lung depends on the windpipe,
but with the intestines, no.
phrases.notes: He means: if the intestines got a hole before the gullet was cut, the animal is a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אֶלָּא בְּרֵיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the limits of the ruling quoted in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency covers only the lung, because it depends on the windpipe. A hole in the intestines still makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the "basket" idea is not a general rule that a cut windpipe ends the slaughter. It applies only to organs whose function depends on the windpipe.

steps.title: Why treat the lung and the intestines differently?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבא. Once the cutting of the windpipe already permits an animal that develops a טרפה sign, there should be no difference between the lung and the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: Once you permitted the animal even though signs of טרפה appeared in it, why should it matter whether the hole was in the lung or in the intestines?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רבא's limit from step 13. He says that if a טרפה sign appearing after the windpipe was cut does not hurt, it should not hurt anywhere in the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said only the lung is 'taken out of the picture,' because it depends on the windpipe. רבי זירא argues that the real reason for the ruling is that the שחיטה had already begun, so a sign that appears afterward should not count. That reason works the same way for the intestines.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a strong challenge to a ruling)
Signs that make an animal a טרפה (a fatal defect)
You permitted
Lung
Intestines

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objects to it:
Since signs of a tereifa developed in it
phrases.notes: He means signs that showed up after the windpipe was already cut.

phrases.english: you permitted [it],
what difference is it to me if it is in the lung,
what difference is it to me if it is in the intestines!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's distinction between the lung and the intestines
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason for permitting is that the טרפה sign appeared after the שחיטה began, that reason applies equally to every organ.

steps.title: רבי זירא takes back his objection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבי זירא retracted. His own question about the intestines being punctured between the two cuts shows that he agrees such a hole does make the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי זירא changed his mind. We know this because he asked: if the intestines were punctured between the cutting of the first סימן and the second סימן, what is the law? Does the first cut join with the second cut to remove the animal from the status of נבלה, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי זירא dropped his challenge to רבא. The proof is a question he asked later on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question assumes that a hole in the intestines between the two cuts does make the animal a טרפה. All he asks is whether the two cuts can still combine to save it from being a נבלה. If he still believed the windpipe cut made the hole harmless, there would be nothing to ask, so his question proves he accepted רבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: And he retracted (changed his mind)
He asked (raised an open question)
Between the cutting of the first סימן (windpipe) and the second (gullet)
Joins together, combines
To make it pure, free from the טומאה of a נבלה

steps.confusionAlert: Being a טרפה and being a נבלה are not the same thing. A טרפה that was properly slaughtered is forbidden to eat but does not carry the טומאה of a נבלה. רבי זירא is asking only about the נבלה status.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Zeira retracted,
as Rabbi Zeira asked:
If the intestines were punctured
between one siman and the other siman, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The two סימנים are the windpipe and the gullet, the two pipes cut in שחיטה.

phrases.aramaic: מִי מִצְטָרֵף סִימָן רִאשׁוֹן לְסִימָן שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: Does the first siman join with the second siman
to purify it from the status of a neveila, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲדַר בֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא, דְּבָעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels רבי זירא's objection from step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי זירא's own objection to רבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His later question shows that he accepted that a hole in the intestines between the cuts makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.title: Is this the same as אילפא's question about a fetus?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי זירא's question is really the same as אילפא's question. אילפא asked about a fetus that put its leg out of the womb between the two cuts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: Isn't this the same as what אילפא asked: if a fetus put out its foreleg between the cutting of the first סימן and the second, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It suggests that רבי זירא's question matches an earlier question asked by אילפא. The discussion continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limb of a fetus that comes out of the womb becomes forbidden like a טרפה. In both cases, something became a טרפה in the middle of the שחיטה. The shared question is whether the two cuts still combine to free it from the status of נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: And we said (the גמרא recalls an earlier discussion)
Isn't this the same as...?
Fetus
Put out its foreleg (out of the womb)

phrases.english: And we said:
Isn't this what Ilfa asked:
If a fetus put out its foreleg
between one siman and the other siman, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares רבי זירא's question in step 15 to an earlier question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי זירא's question about the intestines is identical to אילפא's question about the fetus's foreleg
